issue.body:
The @internal tag (in conjunction with the 'stripInternal' tsconfig
setting) causes this type to be stripped out of the .d.ts files, but it
still needs to be present in the offline compilation case in order to
avoid errors.

Fixes #21456.

See existing discussion on #8819. I don't think the existing tests are running on the .d.ts files that have been stripped of the `@internal`-tagged code. Since fixing that could take substantially more effort than this small regression fix, I am not attempting it in this PR.

body: I have sent out a PR with what I believe is the simplest solution to this regression--removing the `@internal` tag from the type so that it will remain in the relevant .d.ts file and resolve the compilation error.

I believe the original reasoning, per the discussion in the PR, was to avoid littering the public namespace with yet-another type alias. Thus, `ParamsInheritanceStrategy` was used internally for consistency, whereas the external types used the (equivalent) `'emptyOnly'|'always'`.

Does this imply that anything in `pre_activation.ts` is public...?

Thanks @voithos; it sounds like updating `pre_activation.ts` to use `'emptyOnly' | 'always'` in place of `ParamsInheritanceStrategy` would also be another reasonable solution here, then.

> Does this imply that anything in pre_activation.ts is public...?

Check out https://github.com/angular/router-builds/blob/master/src/pre_activation.d.ts to see the declarations produced for `pre_activation.ts`. Is that what you mean? Even though those declarations are not directly part of the router's public API surface, they are still public to consumers of the package, and I believe the use of `ParamsInheritanceStrategy` there is part of the problem.

Ah, that may have been the oversight, then. I think the intent was to keep it internal. Using `'emptyOnly' | 'always'` in `pre_activation.ts` sounds like a reasonable solution, but @IgorMinar would be able to confirm.
